q: How tall is the Shard in London?
hint: For scale: a 10-storey building is about {30 m} tall.
card: When it opened in 2012 it was the tallest building in the European Union.

q: How tall is the Taj Mahal, from the ground to the tip of its dome?
hint: For scale: a giraffe stands about {5.5 m} tall.
card: Its four minarets were built leaning slightly outwards, so in an earthquake they would fall away from the tomb.

q: How tall is the Space Needle in Seattle?
hint: For scale: the Statue of Liberty reaches {93 m} to the tip of its torch.
card: It was built for the 1962 World’s Fair in less than a year.

q: How tall is the CN Tower in Toronto?
hint: For scale: the Eiffel Tower is {330 m} tall with its antennas.
card: It was the world’s tallest free-standing structure for over 30 years.

q: In what year did the Sydney Harbour Bridge open?
hint: For scale: the Titanic sank in 1912.
card: Sydneysiders nicknamed it “the Coathanger” for the shape of its arch.

q: How tall is each president’s head carved into Mount Rushmore?
hint: For scale: a giraffe stands about {5.5 m} tall.
card: Workers carved it between 1927 and 1941, and not one of them died on the job.

q: How long is the Panama Canal, from ocean to ocean?
hint: For scale: a marathon is just over {42 km}.
card: Locks lift ships about 26 m to cross Gatun Lake, then lower them back down to the sea.

q: How tall is the Arc de Triomphe in Paris?
hint: For scale: a 10-storey building is about {30 m} tall.
card: In 1919, three weeks after the First World War victory parade, a pilot flew a biplane through its arch.

q: How tall is the Gateway Arch in St. Louis?
hint: For scale: a football pitch is about {105 m} long.
card: It is exactly as wide between its legs as it is tall.

q: How tall is the Tokyo Skytree?
hint: For scale: the Empire State Building’s roof is {381 m} up.
card: Its official colour, “Skytree White”, is based on aijiro, a traditional Japanese pale blue-white.

q: How tall is the Washington Monument?
hint: For scale: a 30-storey office tower is about {100 m} tall.
card: Its stone changes shade partway up, where building paused for over 20 years.

q: In what year did the London Underground’s first line open?
hint: For scale: the world’s first public steam railway opened in 1825.
card: Its first trains were pulled by steam engines through shallow tunnels dug from the street.

q: How many moons does Mars have?
hint: For scale: Earth has one.
card: They are called Phobos and Deimos, Greek for “fear” and “dread”.

q: How much did Sputnik 1, the first satellite, weigh?
hint: For scale: a grand piano weighs about {300 kg}.
card: It sent out simple radio beeps that amateur radio operators around the world could pick up.

q: How many Earth years does Saturn take to orbit the Sun?
hint: For scale: Jupiter takes about 12 years.
card: Saturn is less dense than water, so in a big enough bathtub it would float.

q: How many Earth days does Venus take to spin once on its axis?
hint: For scale: Earth spins once a day, and Mars takes only slightly longer.
card: That’s longer than its year: Venus goes round the Sun in about 225 Earth days.

q: How many Earths could fit inside Jupiter?
hint: For scale: about 49 Moons would fit inside Earth.
card: Jupiter has more than twice the mass of all the other planets put together.

q: In what year did Halley’s Comet last pass close to Earth?
hint: For scale: Voyager 1 was launched in 1977.
card: It comes back about every 76 years, so its next visit is due in 2061.

q: How far does light travel in one year?
hint: For scale: the Sun is about {150,000,000 km} from Earth.
card: The nearest star beyond the Sun, Proxima Centauri, is about 4.2 light-years away.

q: How far is Mars from the Sun, on average?
hint: For scale: Earth orbits about {150,000,000 km} from the Sun.
card: Its red colour comes from iron oxide, essentially rust, in its dust.

q: How many of the Solar System’s planets have rings?
hint: For scale: the Solar System has eight planets.
card: Saturn’s are by far the brightest; the rings of Jupiter, Uranus and Neptune are faint and dark.

q: In what year did a Space Shuttle first fly into space?
hint: For scale: Apollo 11 landed on the Moon in 1969.
card: The first orbiter to reach space, Columbia, flew with just two astronauts on board.

q: How fast does the International Space Station travel?
hint: For scale: a passenger jet cruises at about {900 km/h}.
card: Its crew sees about 16 sunrises and 16 sunsets every day.

q: How many days did the whole Apollo 11 mission last, launch to splashdown?
hint: For scale: the trip from Earth to the Moon takes about three days.
card: Armstrong and Aldrin spent about 21 hours on the Moon, but only about 2.5 hours walking outside.

q: How many teeth does an adult cat have?
hint: For scale: an adult dog has 42.
card: Kittens start out with 26 smaller milk teeth.

q: How many chromosomes are in a typical human body cell?
hint: For scale: a fruit fly has 8.
card: A potato has 48, two more than we do.

q: How many bones make up the adult human skull?
hint: For scale: one hand and wrist contain 27 bones.
card: Only one of them, the lower jaw, can move freely.

q: How many ribs does a typical adult human have?
hint: For scale: the neck has seven vertebrae.
card: The lowest two pairs are called “floating ribs” because they don’t attach to the breastbone.

q: How many milk teeth does a child have in a full set?
hint: For scale: a full adult set has 32.
card: They start forming before birth, and the first usually appears at around six months old.

q: How much does an ostrich egg weigh?
hint: For scale: a large chicken egg weighs about {0.06 kg}.
card: It is the largest egg of any living bird, yet the smallest compared with the size of the bird.

q: How many days does a chicken egg take to hatch?
hint: For scale: a human pregnancy lasts about 40 weeks.
card: A chick uses a tiny spike on its beak, the egg tooth, to break out of the shell.

q: How tall is General Sherman, the giant sequoia in California?
hint: For scale: a blue whale can grow to about {30 m} long.
card: By volume it is the largest known single-stem tree on Earth.

q: Roughly how many hairs grow on a typical human head?
hint: For scale: a single hair grows about 1 cm a month.
card: Blondes tend to have the most hairs on their heads, and redheads the fewest.

q: In what year was Dolly the sheep, the first mammal cloned from an adult cell, born?
hint: For scale: the World Wide Web went public in 1991.
card: She was named after the singer Dolly Parton.

q: In what year did Charles Darwin publish On the Origin of Species?
hint: For scale: Abraham Lincoln became US president in 1861.
card: Booksellers snapped up the first print run of 1,250 copies before it was even published.

q: Roughly how many quills does a North American porcupine have?
hint: For scale: a hedgehog has around 5,000 spines.
card: Porcupines can’t shoot their quills; they come loose when something touches them.

q: How many years did the Hundred Years’ War between England and France actually last?
hint: For scale: a human lifetime is about 80 years.
card: It ran from 1337 to 1453, though not continuously: long truces broke up the fighting.

q: How many people signed the US Declaration of Independence?
hint: For scale: the US Senate has 100 members.
card: John Hancock signed so large that “John Hancock” became American slang for a signature.

q: For how many years did Queen Victoria reign?
hint: For scale: a typical working life is about 40 years.
card: Her record as Britain’s longest-reigning monarch stood until Elizabeth II passed it in 2015.

q: In what year did people first reach the South Pole?
hint: For scale: Queen Victoria died in 1901.
card: Roald Amundsen’s Norwegian team beat Robert Falcon Scott’s British team there by about five weeks.

q: In what year was the first Harry Potter book published?
hint: For scale: the first Toy Story film came out in 1995.
card: Its first UK print run was just 500 copies.

q: In what year did Mickey Mouse first appear on screen in Steamboat Willie?
hint: For scale: the Empire State Building opened in 1931.
card: It was one of the first cartoons with fully synchronised sound, and Walt Disney voiced Mickey himself.

q: In what year was the first Star Wars film released?
hint: For scale: Jaws, often called the first summer blockbuster, came out in 1975.
card: Darth Vader’s voice was dubbed by James Earl Jones, who at first went uncredited.

q: In what year did the United States buy Alaska from Russia?
hint: For scale: the American Civil War ended in 1865.
card: The price worked out at about two cents per acre.

q: In what year was the first FIFA World Cup played?
hint: For scale: the first modern Olympics were held in 1896.
card: Uruguay hosted and won it, beating Argentina 4–2 in the final.

q: In what year was Tutankhamun’s tomb discovered?
hint: For scale: the First World War ended in 1918.
card: Howard Carter’s team spent about ten years cataloguing the more than 5,000 objects inside.

q: In what year were the first Nobel Prizes awarded?
hint: For scale: Alfred Nobel died in 1896.
card: Wilhelm Röntgen won the first physics prize, for discovering X-rays.

q: In what year did euro notes and coins first go into circulation?
hint: For scale: the euro first existed as an electronic currency in 1999.
card: Twelve countries switched their cash at once, the biggest currency changeover in history.

q: In what year did Charles Lindbergh fly solo nonstop across the Atlantic?
hint: For scale: the Wright brothers first flew in 1903.
card: The flight from New York to Paris took about 33.5 hours, with no co-pilot to take over.

q: What is the most passengers an Airbus A380 is certified to carry?
hint: For scale: a Boeing 737 seats about 160 to 190.
card: Its upper deck runs the full length of the plane, making it the largest passenger airliner ever built.

q: How many strings does a modern concert harp have?
hint: For scale: a standard guitar has six.
card: Its red strings mark every C and its black or blue strings every F, so harpists can find their place.

q: In what year did Nintendo release the first Game Boy?
hint: For scale: the Rubik’s Cube was invented in 1974.
card: Bundled with Tetris outside Japan, it and the Game Boy Color sold over 118 million units.

q: In what year did Alexander Graham Bell patent the telephone?
hint: For scale: the first transatlantic telegraph cable carried messages in 1858.
card: His first words over it were “Mr. Watson, come here, I want to see you.”

q: How tall was the Saturn V moon rocket?
hint: For scale: the Statue of Liberty reaches {93 m} to the tip of its torch.
card: It carried 24 astronauts toward the Moon over nine crewed missions.

q: How many wheels are on a Boeing 747’s landing gear?
hint: For scale: a typical car has four.
card: Sixteen sit on four main gear legs, two under the wings and two under the body, plus two on the nose gear.

q: How many Ford Model T cars were built?
hint: For scale: Volkswagen built about 21.5 million original Beetles.
card: For years it came in any colour you liked, as long as it was black.

q: In what year did Sony launch the first Walkman?
hint: For scale: the compact cassette tape was introduced in 1963.
card: Sony built the first one so a co-founder could listen to music on long flights.

q: How long was the Titanic?
hint: For scale: a football pitch is about {105 m} long.
card: Of its four funnels, only three vented smoke; the fourth was mostly for ventilation and looks.

q: How long was the Hindenburg airship?
hint: For scale: a Boeing 747 is about {70 m} long.
card: It and its sister ship remain the longest aircraft ever to fly.

q: How many spaces run around the edge of a Monopoly board?
hint: For scale: a chessboard has 64 squares.
card: The four corners are Go, Jail, Free Parking and Go to Jail.

q: How high is a basketball hoop’s rim above the floor?
hint: For scale: a typical room ceiling is about {2.4 m} high.
card: James Naismith’s first hoop, in 1891, was a peach basket nailed to a raised running track.

q: How long is a cricket pitch, from wicket to wicket?
hint: For scale: a double-decker bus is about {11 m} long.
card: The length is one chain, an old surveyor’s unit of 22 yards.

q: How many tiles come in a standard English Scrabble set, blanks included?
hint: For scale: a deck of cards has 52.
card: There’s only one Q and one Z, each worth ten points.

q: How heavy is a standard men’s Olympic weightlifting bar, without plates?
hint: For scale: a car tyre weighs about {10 kg}.
card: It is 2.2 m long; the women’s bar is a little shorter and lighter.

q: How long is a tennis court, from baseline to baseline?
hint: For scale: a basketball court is about {28 m} long.
card: The net sags in the middle, where it is about 15 cm lower than at the posts.

q: How many lines does a traditional sonnet have?
hint: For scale: a limerick has five.
card: Shakespeare wrote 154 of them.

q: How many coloured stickers cover a standard 3×3 Rubik’s Cube?
hint: For scale: a die has six faces.
card: It can be scrambled in about 43 quintillion ways, yet any position can be solved in 20 moves.

q: What is the highest score possible with three darts?
hint: For scale: the bullseye is worth 50.
card: Players call it a “ton 80”: three darts in the treble 20.

q: What is the maximum break in snooker under normal circumstances?
hint: For scale: a snooker frame starts with 15 red balls.
card: Ronnie O’Sullivan made one in just 5 minutes 8 seconds in 1997.

q: How high is the crossbar of a full-size soccer goal?
hint: For scale: a typical interior door is about {2 m} tall.
card: Goal sizes come from old British units: 8 feet high and 8 yards wide.
